title: 21yo M Dengue Shock Syndrome
chiefComplaint: Fever for 5 days, now cold and drowsy
background: Rice farmer from Pak Thong Chai. Five days of high fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgia and vomiting. The fever broke this morning and the family thought he was improving, then he became cold, clammy and confused. Two neighbours have had dengue this month. No comorbidities. He took an unknown NSAID from the village shop for four days.

exam.finding: Restless then drowsy, cold clammy peripheries despite being afebrile, narrow pulse pressure of 10 mmHg
Flushed face, injected conjunctivae, gum bleeding on gentle probing, no neck stiffness, dry tongue
Sinus tachycardia, weak thready pulse, capillary refill 5 seconds, narrow pulse pressure, heart sounds normal
Reduced air entry at the right base with stony dull percussion, consistent with pleural effusion from plasma leak
Tender hepatomegaly 3 cm below the costal margin, shifting dullness, no rebound, severe abdominal pain is a dengue warning sign
Confluent blanching rash with islands of sparing over both legs, scattered petechiae, positive tourniquet test, cool mottled knees
GCS 13 (E3V4M6), no focal deficit, no meningism, pupils equal and reactive

investigations.name: Haematocrit
investigations.report: Rise of more than 20% above baseline of 43%. This is the marker of plasma leakage and the number you titrate fluid against.

investigations.name: Platelet count
investigations.report: Severe thrombocytopenia. Do not transfuse platelets in the absence of significant bleeding, it does not improve outcome.

investigations.name: Dengue NS1 antigen and IgM
investigations.report: Confirms acute dengue. He is in the critical phase, which begins as the fever falls.

investigations.name: AST and ALT
investigations.report: Transaminitis with AST above ALT, typical of dengue. Severe hepatitis is a severe dengue criterion.

investigations.name: Bedside ultrasound
investigations.report: Right pleural effusion, gallbladder wall thickening to 8 mm, small volume ascites and a collapsible inferior vena cava. Plasma leak with intravascular depletion.

distractors.label: The fever has gone, so tell the family he is recovering
distractors.feedback: Defervescence marks the start of the critical phase in dengue, when plasma leak and shock occur.

distractors.label: Wait for the dengue IgM result before deciding on treatment
distractors.feedback: Management is clinical. A baseline haematocrit and shock assessment guide fluids now.

data.label: Recognise the critical phase and get a baseline haematocrit
actions: Bedside ultrasound for effusion and ascites

distractors.label: Give platelets because the count is low
distractors.feedback: Prophylactic platelets do not prevent bleeding or shock in dengue. The shock is from plasma leak and needs crystalloid.

distractors.label: Hold all fluids because he may get pulmonary oedema
distractors.feedback: He is in compensated shock now. He needs an isotonic bolus, then a careful step-down.

data.label: Dextrose isotonic bolus for compensated shock

doseMap.5%D/NSS bolus: 500 mL over 1 to 2 hours in an adult, 10 mL/kg in a child, as in the Thai Department of Medical Services dengue guideline. Thai wards use dextrose-containing isotonic fluid such as 5%D/NSS. Reassess haematocrit, pulse pressure and urine output after it.

data.choice: Stop the NSAID, no IM injections

distractors.label: Continue the NSAID for the myalgia and fever
distractors.feedback: NSAIDs increase bleeding risk and gastritis in dengue. Use paracetamol only.

distractors.label: IM diclofenac for the pain
distractors.feedback: IM injections cause haematomas in dengue, and NSAIDs worsen bleeding. Avoid both.

data.label: Stop the NSAID and avoid intramuscular injections

doseMap.Paracetamol for fever: 500 mg orally every 6 hours, maximum 2 g/day given the transaminitis

data.label: Partial response
data.narrative: Pulse pressure widens to 22 mmHg after the second bolus. Haematocrit falls to 48%. He is warmer and more alert but urine output is only 0.3 mL/kg/h.

data.label: Explain to the family why he got worse after the fever broke (Empathy)
data.narrative: The family believed the falling fever meant recovery and nearly took him home this morning. You explain that dengue is most dangerous in the 24 to 48 hours after defervescence. They immediately understand, and they tell you the neighbour's daughter is at home with the same story on day five. Pi Jai sends a message to the village health volunteer.

data.choice: Step fluids down, titrate to urine and haematocrit

distractors.label: Keep running 20 mL/kg/h until the blood pressure is normal
distractors.feedback: Over-resuscitation causes fluid overload and pulmonary oedema as plasma leak ends. Step fluids down and titrate to urine output and haematocrit.

distractors.label: Stop all IV fluids now that he has responded
distractors.feedback: The leak continues for 24 to 48 hours. Abrupt cessation risks recurrent shock. Taper the rate.

data.label: Titrate to urine output and haematocrit, not to blood pressure alone

doseMap.Step down 250, 150, 100, 80, then 40 mL/: The adult step-down in the Thai guideline, one step at a time as vital signs and haematocrit allow. Aim for urine output of 0.5 mL/kg/h. Across the 24 to 48 hour leak the total should stay near maintenance plus 5% deficit, the M+5% Thai wards are taught to respect.
doseMap.Haematocrit every 4 to 6 hours: The critical phase interval in the Thai guideline. A rising haematocrit means more leak. A falling haematocrit with unstable vital signs means hidden bleeding.

data.label: Reabsorption phase
data.narrative: At 30 hours his haematocrit drops to 38%, urine output rises and the rash becomes confluent and itchy. Fluids are stopped. Platelets are 24 and rising. He never needed a transfusion.

distractors.label: Discharge home with paracetamol now that he has responded
distractors.feedback: He is still within the critical phase. Admit for monitoring until the leak resolves.

distractors.label: Admit without observations to let him sleep
distractors.feedback: The critical phase needs close monitoring for shock, bleeding and fluid overload.

data.label: Admit for monitored observation through the critical phase
actions: Watch for fluid overload and pulmonary oedema

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Discharged on day 8 with a platelet count of 96 and no bleeding. Vector control is notified. The neighbour's daughter arrives that evening in early shock and is caught in time.
